raw:
Scientific Specialist — signal: caution

{
  "verdict_signal": "caution",
  "concerns": [
    "The genetic arms are reasonable in structure (CRISPR KO plus two independent siRNAs, scrambled and vehicle controls, WT rescue) but the WT rescue alone does not separate the nominal target from an off-pathway consequence: it confirms the phenotype is NSMCE3-dependent, not that it runs through NSMCE3's catalytic/enzymatic function. Without the catalytically-dead rescue, a scaffolding or complex-stoichiometry effect is indistinguishable from the mechanism claimed.",
    "NSMCE3 is an obligate component of the SMC5/6 complex; loss of it destabilises NSMCE2/SMC5/SMC6 and produces broad genome-instability phenotypes. Any KO or knockdown therefore has a large, non-specific downstream footprint, which makes the attribution problem here worse than for a standalone enzyme. Complex-partner levels after KO/knockdown appear not to have been measured.",
    "The unmeasured paralogue is a live confounder, not a theoretical one — it is the single most likely explanation for a phenotype that survives target loss or for the tool compound's 800 nM activity, and the PI has flagged it as unmeasured.",
    "The tool compound is not corroborating evidence at present: 12-fold selectivity against only two family members, a phenol (redox-cycling and quinone-forming liability, a common source of apparent target-independent cytotoxicity), and no proteomic or thermal-shift engagement data. Pharmacological and genetic arms converging is the usual independent check, and that check is currently unavailable.",
    "n=6 per arm with a post hoc, non-pre-specified analysis. For a robust genetic phenotype this may be adequate, but it gives no protection against selective endpoint reporting, and no effect size or variance was quoted to judge power.",
    "Single laboratory, single set of hands, no external replication. Utrecht has requested reagents but has not yet run anything.",
    "\"Two primary human explants, both responded\" is n=2 donors — encouraging but not a translatability claim. Mouse and human curves within ~5-fold is a weak concordance statement without knowing which direction and on which endpoint; SMC5/6 biology and the interferon/HBV-restriction functions of the complex differ between species."
  ],
  "questions_to_ask": [
    "When you knock out NSMCE3, what happens to SMC5, SMC6 and NSMCE2 protein levels? If the whole complex falls apart, how do you know you are looking at NSMCE3 rather than at generalised SMC5/6 loss?",
    "What is the catalytically-dead construct — which residues, and what is the expected effect on complex assembly? If the dead mutant still assembles into the complex and still rescues, what would you conclude?",
    "Does your tool compound phenocopy the genetic loss in the KO background? If the compound still kills NSMCE3-null cells at 800 nM, that tells us the cell death is off-target — have you run that experiment?",
    "You mentioned the paralogue as a possible confounder. What would you predict if you knocked it down alone, and in combination with NSMCE3?",
    "What was the effect size and variance in the n=6 experiments, and how many endpoints did you look at before settling on the one you published?",
    "For the two human explants — what were the donor characteristics, and were they run blinded? Would you be willing to specify the primary endpoint and the analysis in advance for the next set?",
    "What exactly would you send Utrecht, and what would you want them to try to reproduce first? Would you accept their result if it were negative?",
    "Is the phenol required for activity, or have you tested a close analogue without it to rule out redox artefact?"
  ],
  "confidence": "moderate"
}

Chemistry Specialist — signal: caution

{
  "verdict_signal": "caution",
  "concerns": [
    "The entire chemical estate is a single commercial library hit at 800 nM cellular with no measured biochemical potency — there is no SAR series, so nothing is known about whether the chemotype responds to structural change at all; tractability is currently an assumption, not an observation",
    "Free phenol on the hit is a recognised liability cluster: glucuronidation/sulfation-driven clearance, quinone-methide or quinone-imine reactive metabolite risk depending on substitution, and it is often the pharmacophore-critical group, meaning the first medchem question (can we cap or bioisosterically replace it) may not have an answer that retains potency",
    "12-fold selectivity against two family members is a lead-finding starting point, not a selectivity margin — and the family was not enumerated: NSMCE3 sits in the SMC5/6 complex context, so the relevant liability set includes complex partners and the unmeasured paralogue the PI himself flagged as a confounder in the biology",
    "The paralogue has not been measured either in the biology or in the compound profile, so it is unresolved whether the 800 nM cellular effect is on-target NSMCE3 engagement, paralogue cross-inhibition, or an off-pathway cytotoxic effect — no target-engagement biomarker or catalytically-dead rescue exists to distinguish these",
    "No PK, no tox, no solubility, no permeability, no plasma protein binding — and glioblastoma imposes CNS penetration as a hard, non-negotiable design constraint (free brain/plasma Kp,uu, P-gp/BCRP efflux) that has not been assessed for this chemotype and can kill an otherwise good series",
    "No therapeutic index data of any kind in any species, so there is no basis to judge whether a tolerated CNS-penetrant exposure could reach the ~800 nM (unoptimised) cellular level, let alone with margin",
    "No composition-of-matter position — the provisional is method-of-use only — which means whatever series a medchem campaign produces has to be patentable de novo from a commercial library scaffold that may already be claimed",
    "No in-house medchem capability, one postdoc departing in 18 months, no staff scientist, and no costed plan for the campaign that the PI correctly says is required — the chemistry risk is structurally unmanageable from the current resource base regardless of how tractable the chemotype turns out to be",
    "Mechanistically it is not stated whether NSMCE3 presents a druggable small-molecule pocket at all: if the biology runs through protein-protein interaction within the SMC5/6 complex rather than an enzymatic active site, orthosteric small-molecule inhibition may be the wrong modality and no alternative (degrader, PPI stabiliser) has been considered"
  ],
  "questions_to_ask": [
    "What is the actual structure of the library hit, and is the phenol part of the pharmacophore — have you made even one methyl ether or a single bioisostere (F, CN, difluoromethyl, oxetane) to see whether potency survives capping it?",
    "Do you have a biochemical or binding assay for NSMCE3, or is 800 nM purely a cellular phenotypic readout? If cellular only, how do you know the compound is engaging NSMCE3 rather than the paralogue or something off-pathway entirely?",
    "Does the compound's cellular effect disappear in your CRISPR KO cells? That single experiment would tell us whether we are optimising against the target or against a cytotoxic artefact.",
    "Which family members were the two you tested at 12-fold, and where does the unmeasured paralogue sit — have you run the compound against it, given you already identified it as a confounder in the biology?",
    "Is there a structure — crystal, cryo-EM, or a credible model — of the NSMCE3 site you think the compound binds? Is this an enzymatic pocket or are we trying to break a protein-protein interface inside the SMC5/6 complex?",
    "Have you looked at any of the neighbours around the hit in the vendor catalogue — did you buy five or ten analogues to see whether there is any SAR at all, or is this literally a single point?",
    "For recurrent GBM the compound has to get into brain: has anyone measured solubility, LogD, TPSA, or run even a rough MDCK-MDR1 efflux screen on this chemotype? What is your read on whether this scaffold can be made CNS-penetrant?",
    "What free brain concentration do you think you need, and how does that compare to the 800 nM cellular number — is there any plausible dose that clears that bar with a safety margin?",
    "Has the hit been checked against PAINS filters and run in a redox-cycling or thiol-reactivity assay? Phenols in phenotypic screens are the classic false-positive class and I want to rule that out before anyone commits medchem FTE.",
    "If NSMCE3 turns out to have no tractable pocket, what is your fallback modality — a degrader, a peptide, something else — and is that a considered choice or a retreat from chemistry that did not work?",
    "Who would actually run the medchem campaign, on what scaffold, and with what composition-of-matter position, given the provisional is method-of-use only and the starting point came out of a commercial catalogue?"
  ],
  "confidence": "moderate"
}

Clinical Specialist — signal: caution

{
  "verdict_signal": "caution",
  "concerns": [
    "Recurrent GBM is a genuine unmet need — lomustine gives roughly 8-9 months median OS with response rates in the single digits — so the gap is real, but that same graveyard means preclinical ranking has historically had almost no predictive value here; dozens of agents with clean mouse efficacy have failed, so a favourable preclinical ranking is not the decision point developers act on.",
    "In practice the gating question for rGBM developers is not target rank but CNS exposure: free brain concentration, P-gp/BCRP efflux ratio, and behaviour in non-enhancing tumour where the blood-brain barrier is intact. The PI has no PK at all, so the program cannot yet be ranked against competitors on the axis that actually determines go/no-go.",
    "The indication as stated is unstratified 'recurrent glioblastoma'. NSMCE3 sits in the SMC5/6 genome-stability complex, which points naturally toward a synthetic-lethal or DNA-damage-context population — MGMT-methylated, alkylator-pretreated, or an HR/ATRX-defective slice. No biomarker hypothesis has been articulated, and an all-comers rGBM trial is the least informative and highest-attrition design available.",
    "The PI does not know the incidence numbers. rGBM is ~13,000 new GBM diagnoses/year in the US, nearly all of whom recur, but the trial-eligible, KPS-adequate, biomarker-selected fraction is a small subset — a stratified design needs to be costed against enrolment feasibility across a multi-site network, and that arithmetic has not been done.",
    "Standard-of-care drift is real: TTFields is in the frontline guideline, the IDH-mutant space has been reshaped by vorasidenib (which pulls a distinct population out of the glioma pool), and Chimerix's dordaviprone/ONC201 activity in H3K27M-altered glioma has set an expectation that new CNS agents arrive with a molecular selection marker. Arriving in 6-8 years with an unstratified rGBM asset is arriving into a stratified field.",
    "The regulatory path as framed is the unfavourable one: unstratified rGBM with OS endpoints and no interim biomarker readout. A defined genetic subgroup would open accelerated approval on ORR/PFS6 with a much smaller n — that path exists and is not being taken."
  ],
  "questions_to_ask": [
    "If NSMCE3 sits in the SMC5/6 genome-stability complex, is there a DNA-repair context that makes tumour cells dependent on it — MGMT-methylated, alkylator-pretreated, ATRX-loss, HR-deficient? Put another way: which glioblastoma patient would you predict responds, and which one would you predict does not?",
    "Have you tested the tool compound, or any NSMCE3 knockdown, in an orthotopic intracranial model rather than flank — and do you have any measurement of free drug in brain tissue versus plasma?",
    "Your two human explants — what was their molecular profile (IDH status, MGMT methylation, prior temozolomide exposure), and did the two responders share anything that the tumour bank's non-responders would lack?",
    "Is there a reason NSMCE3 dependency should be greater in recurrent than in newly diagnosed disease, or is rGBM simply the indication where the regulatory bar for a first trial is lowest?",
    "If the mechanism is genome-instability-driven, is glioblastoma actually the best first indication, or is there a peripheral tumour with a cleaner genetic definition — where you could establish proof of mechanism without also having to solve blood-brain-barrier penetration at the same time?",
    "What would you expect this to be combined with? Lomustine and temozolomide are both alkylators — does an SMC5/6 mechanism synergise with them, or does the overlapping myelosuppression make that combination undeliverable?"
  ],
  "confidence": "moderate"
}

Commercial Specialist — signal: caution

{
  "verdict_signal": "caution",
  "concerns": [
    "The competitive landscape is essentially unassessed: the PI names one program (Chimerix, presumably dordaviprone/ONC201 or the older brincidofovir-era assets) and concedes no systematic landscape has been done. A single anecdotal comparator is not a landscape, and the hub cannot price differentiation off it.",
    "The differentiation claim is target novelty, not asset novelty. NSMCE3 (NDNL2, SMC5/6 complex) has essentially no disclosed small-molecule programs — which is a first-in-class story only if the reason is undruggability-now-solved rather than nobody-wants-it. Nothing presented distinguishes those two cases, and the SMC5/6 complex has a well-known liability profile as a genome-stability/DNA-repair node with likely broad proliferative toxicity.",
    "Recurrent glioblastoma is the single most crowded and most investor-fatigued oncology indication relative to its commercial return. Lomustine-comparator rGBM is where assets go to generate signal-seeking Phase 2s and then fail; the graveyard (ONC201 outside H3K27M, VAL-083, depatuxizumab mafodotin, rindopepimut, and the broad DDR-inhibitor cohort) is directly on point. Choosing rGBM as the lead indication actively subtracts value from a novel-target story rather than adding to it.",
    "The IP shape is the wrong shape for a license. A method-of-use provisional on a target-pathway link, no composition-of-matter, no national-phase decision, and a commercial-library tool compound with a phenol means there is no proprietary chemical matter to license. Buyers of preclinical oncology assets pay for composition-of-matter; target-pathway method-of-use claims on their own price near zero and are routinely designed around.",
    "The asset sits below the stage at which meaningful deal comparables exist. Precedent oncology target-validation licenses at this stage (no lead, no PK, no tox, unreplicated mechanism, single-lab paper) are option/research-collaboration structures with low-to-mid-six-figure upfronts and biobucks — not the multi-year, multi-programme financing the PI gestures at without costing.",
    "The DDR/genome-stability space specifically has cooled: post-PARP, investors have watched WEE1, ATR, and PKMYT1 programmes struggle on therapeutic index. A new SMC5/6-adjacent target enters into that sentiment, not into a vacuum.",
    "The platform claim (screen generalises, one unpublished second target) is asserted with no evidence the hub can weigh, and platform framing on a single validated output does not create venture-scale shape — it usually signals the single asset is too thin to stand alone.",
    "Single-lab, unreplicated mechanism with an outside group only now requesting reagents means any counterparty's first diligence step is independent replication. That is a 9-18 month gate before commercial conversations can even begin, and the Utrecht replication is currently the highest-leverage commercial event in the file, uncontrolled by the PI."
  ],
  "questions_to_ask": [
    "Search patent filings and clinical registries for any disclosed small-molecule, degrader, or oligonucleotide programme against NSMCE3/NDNL2 or any SMC5/6 complex subunit — if there are genuinely none from industry, what is the documented reason? Has any pharma publicly deprioritised SMC5/6 as a target, and on what grounds (essentiality, therapeutic index, tractability)?",
    "What is the actual bear case on SMC5/6 as an oncology target? Pull the DepMap/Project Score common-essentiality calls for NSMCE3 and the complex: if it scores as pan-essential, this is a first-in-class claim for a reason that no medchem campaign fixes, and we should know that before spending anything.",
    "Build the honest rGBM comparable set for the last ten years: for assets that entered rGBM with a novel target and a lomustine-controlled design, what were the licensing terms at preclinical stage, what fraction reached Phase 3, and what did the failures cost their partners? We need to know whether rGBM is a value-creating first indication or a value-destroying one before we let the PI keep it.",
    "What have preclinical target-validation-only oncology deals with no composition-of-matter actually transacted for in the last five years? Find the structures — option-to-license, research collaboration, straight assignment — and the upfronts, so we can test whether the 'low hundreds of thousands over two years' the PI wants is even recoverable at exit.",
    "Which acquirers or licensors are currently buying DDR/genome-stability assets at all, versus which have publicly exited the space? If the natural buyer list for a SMC5/6 asset is thin or shrinking, the differentiation is commercially irrelevant regardless of how real the biology is.",
    "Is there a non-GBM indication where an SMC5/6 or DNA-damage-repair mechanism has a better-established commercial path — for example a synthetic-lethal context with a defined biomarker population? If a repositioning exists, the whole commercial shape changes and the rGBM framing is a self-inflicted wound.",
    "What exactly is the Chimerix rGBM programme's current status, mechanism, and market reception, and does it compete with or validate this? The PI has named it without analysis; we should establish whether it is a comparable, a competitor, or a cautionary tale.",
    "If the target-pathway method-of-use claim is the only IP, can a competitor with better chemistry practise around it by simply not claiming the mechanism? Get a commercial read on whether this filing has any blocking value at all, independent of the formal FTO/patentability work another reviewer owns."
  ],
  "confidence": "moderate"
}

Legal Specialist — signal: caution

{
  "verdict_signal": "caution",
  "concerns": [
    "No FTO opinion of any kind has been obtained; the PI states this explicitly. Absence of a systematic landscape search is not evidence of freedom to operate, particularly in a crowded DNA-damage-response/SMC5/6 space.",
    "The only filing is a January provisional on target-pathway link, method-of-use, no composition of matter. Priority is under 12 months old and the TTO has not committed to national phase — there is a real risk the priority lapses or is narrowed before Blackbird's diligence completes.",
    "A method-of-use claim over a target-pathway link is the weakest ownable position available: it does not exclude a competitor who arrives at a different chemical series against NSMCE3, and it is vulnerable to the published JBC paper being read as enabling disclosure of the mechanism itself.",
    "The mechanism was published in J Biol Chem last year. If the provisional was filed in January and the publication preceded it, the PI's own paper may be prior art against the very claims filed — the publication/filing chronology has not been established and is material.",
    "The tool compound came from a commercial library. Commercial screening libraries are routinely supplied under terms carrying field-of-use restrictions or hit-reporting/option obligations to the supplier; if the compound or a close analogue anchors the programme, the supplier's terms may reach into it. The library source and its terms have not been disclosed.",
    "Two primary human explants were used. Human tissue carries consent-scope and IRB limitations that frequently exclude commercial exploitation; whether the consent covers for-profit downstream use is unaddressed.",
    "The screen the PI proposes as a generalisable platform is unpublished and its provenance is undocumented — if any component (library, reporter line, assay construct) came in under an MTA with reach-through, the platform claim is encumbered independently of the NSMCE3 asset.",
    "CRISPR use is stated. Depending on the editing system employed, third-party licences (Broad/Berkeley or vendor-limited research-only terms) may be needed for any commercial application beyond generating research data, though this is typically manageable rather than blocking.",
    "The Utrecht group has requested reagents. An outbound transfer executed on institutional standard terms without an option or publication-review carve-out could create a competing filer or a co-inventorship dispute; whether an MTA is in place and on what terms is unknown.",
    "Co-inventorship has not been probed at all. The PI asserts 'one lab, our own hands', but a departing postdoc, a rotating student, and two other concurrently running R01s create both inventorship questions and funding-attribution questions (which grant funded which experiments, and therefore whose Bayh-Dole obligations and march-in exposure attach)."
  ],
  "questions_to_ask": [
    "Which commercial library did the tool compound come from, and can you send us the supplier's terms and conditions or purchase agreement as executed?",
    "Can you list every reagent, plasmid, cell line, antibody, and mouse strain in this work that arrived from outside your institution, and identify which came in under an MTA?",
    "Was the JBC paper published before or after the January provisional filing date — can you give us both dates?",
    "Who are the named inventors on the January provisional, and does that list include the postdoc and the rotating student?",
    "Which of your grants funded the NSMCE3 work specifically, and were any of the experiments in the JBC paper supported by either of the other two R01s?",
    "Under what consent and IRB protocol were the two human explants obtained, and does that consent permit commercial use of derived data?",
    "Has anything gone to the Utrecht group yet, and if so under what agreement?",
    "For the unpublished screen you describe as generalisable — where did the screening library, reporter line, and assay constructs originate?",
    "Which CRISPR system and reagent source did you use for the knockout?",
    "Has the TTO given you a date by which it must decide on national phase, and can we speak to the licensing officer directly?"
  ],
  "confidence": "moderate"
}

Technologic Specialist — signal: blocking

{
  "verdict_signal": "blocking",
  "concerns": [
    "The platform claim rests on n=1 completed application (NSMCE3) plus one unpublished, uncharacterised run on 'one other target class' with no stated hit criteria, hit rate, or validation — that is an anecdote, not a demonstrated generalisation.",
    "The screen's operating characteristics are entirely undescribed: no false-positive/false-negative rate, no benchmarking against known-positive controls, no statement of what target classes it can and cannot address. Without these there is no way to predict performance on target #3.",
    "Zero independent reproduction: the underlying biology is one lab, one set of hands, and the Utrecht group has only requested reagents. Screen reproducibility outside this lab is untested, which is the single most common failure mode for method-based platform claims.",
    "The proposed work as described advances the NSMCE3 product line (cat-dead rescue, paralogue measurement, medchem) — none of which tests the screen's generalisability. A successful outcome would leave the platform claim exactly where it is today.",
    "No articulated failure mode for the platform: the PI has not said what result on a second or third target would cause him to conclude the screen does not generalise, so a negative is likely to be absorbed as 'that target was hard' rather than as platform-limiting.",
    "Transferable assets are unclear. It is not stated whether what generalises is a written protocol, a specific reagent/library, an analysis pipeline, or the PI's judgement in picking targets — the last is not a platform.",
    "Team structure cannot sustain a platform demonstration: no staff scientist, postdoc departs in 18 months, and the tacit know-how for the screen therefore sits in one person with a fixed expiry date."
  ],
  "questions_to_ask": [
    "Set NSMCE3 aside for a moment — describe the screen itself. What is the input, what is the readout, what classes of target does it work for, and what have you tried it on where it did not work?",
    "You mentioned running it on one other target class and getting 'something interesting'. What was the hit rate, what were the criteria for calling a hit, and has any of it been validated by an orthogonal method yet?",
    "If I gave you a target you had never seen and a blinded set of positive and negative controls, would you expect the screen to recover the positives? Has anyone ever run it that way?",
    "What exactly would you hand the Utrecht group — a written SOP, a reagent set, a plasmid library, an analysis script? And if they run it and get nothing, what would that tell you about the method versus about them?",
    "What result, on which target, would make you say the screen does not generalise? I want a specific outcome you would accept as platform-limiting rather than target-specific.",
    "Of the two years you are proposing, how much is NSMCE3 and how much is a second, independent target run end-to-end? If the answer is zero on the second, what is the basis for calling this a platform rather than a project?",
    "Your postdoc leaves in eighteen months. Is the screen documented well enough that someone new could run it from the protocol alone, or does it currently live in that person's hands?"
  ],
  "confidence": "high"
}

Talent Specialist — signal: caution

{
  "verdict_signal": "caution",
  "concerns": [
    "Team is effectively 1.5 FTE of bench capacity: one postdoc departing in 18 months and one rotating student, against a workplan that includes a catalytically-dead rescue, paralogue measurement, human explant work, and an externally-sourced medchem campaign",
    "No succession depth — if the PI is unavailable there is no named co-investigator or staff scientist, and the postdoc's departure inside the project window means the only trained pair of hands leaves mid-stream with no stated replacement or handover plan",
    "PI carries two active R01s with no stated effort allocation; bandwidth for a third program is asserted rather than demonstrated",
    "Team lacks medicinal chemistry entirely and the PI concedes the campaign cannot be run in-house, but no named CRO, collaborator, or core facility has been identified — this is a capability gap with no fill plan",
    "No prior track record cited for a project of this type: the JBC paper was a single-lab mechanism study, not a translational package with chemistry, PK, and tox milestones, so comparable-scope execution is unestablished",
    "Reagent-sharing request from Utrecht is unmanaged; no stated collaboration structure that would either extend capacity or protect the timeline",
    "Absence of a costed budget makes it impossible to verify that the proposed staffing is even affordable — flagging as an execution-credibility signal, though budget scope itself is not mine"
  ],
  "questions_to_ask": [
    "Walk me through your calendar: what percent effort are you committing to this, and where does it come from given the two R01s — are you buying out teaching, or is something else winding down?",
    "Your postdoc leaves in eighteen months. Who does the work in months nineteen through twenty-four, and when would you need to start recruiting to have them trained before the handover?",
    "You've said the medchem campaign can't run in-house. Name the CRO or academic collaborator you'd use, and tell me whether you've had a scoping conversation with them yet or whether this is still hypothetical.",
    "If you were hit by a bus tomorrow, who in your institution could pick up this project and finish it? Is there anyone who currently understands the assay well enough to run it without you?",
    "Have you ever run a project with an external chemistry partner and a multi-workstream timeline before? What was it, and did it land on schedule?",
    "The Utrecht group wants your reagents. Is there a version of this where they become a formal co-investigator and absorb some of the replication and paralogue work, or do you want to keep it in-house?",
    "Of the deliverables in this package — dead rescue, paralogue quantification, explant expansion, PK — which one do you personally do with your own hands, and which are you assuming someone you haven't hired yet will do?"
  ],
  "confidence": "moderate"
}

Budget Specialist — signal: caution

{
  "verdict_signal": "caution",
  "concerns": [
    "The stated ask (low hundreds of thousands over two years) is not a costed budget — it is a guess, so there is no basis for judging burn-to-milestone at all.",
    "Scope overrun is the core issue: the PI names an outsourced medchem campaign as necessary for a real lead. A hit-to-lead campaign is a $1M+ multi-year line item on its own and does not fit inside a $100K–$1M incubation grant that must also fund the catalytically-dead rescue, paralogue measurement, PK, and tox.",
    "If the ask is genuinely ~$200–400K over 24 months, that is a proof-of-concept band being asked to carry a development program. Either the scope must shrink to biology validation only, or the vehicle must be re-framed — the two as stated are inconsistent.",
    "n=6 per arm was described as 'what the budget allowed'. If the confirmatory work needs to be adequately powered and pre-registered, replication cost is a real and unpriced line, not a rounding error.",
    "Duration risk is concrete rather than abstract: the only experienced pair of hands leaves at month 18 of a 24-month plan, and there is no staff scientist line budgeted to cover the tail.",
    "Follow-on is entirely unplanned — the PI has not identified who funds the next stage. There is no named target for the raise, no sense of what milestone would unlock it, and therefore no accounting for the bridge period while that raise happens.",
    "The unfunded IP path (TTO undecided on national phase, no FTO opinion) is a cost that lands inside this window and is not in the guessed number."
  ],
  "questions_to_ask": [
    "If we told you the money available is $400K over 24 months and not a dollar more, what would you cut, and what single result would you commit to delivering by month 24?",
    "Can you separate the work into what you can do with your own hands versus what has to be bought from a CRO, and put a price on each half? The medchem campaign in particular — is that inside this ask or outside it?",
    "Your postdoc leaves at month 18. Walk me through months 18 to 24: who is at the bench, and is that person in the budget?",
    "Assume the confirmatory package works. Who writes the next cheque, roughly how big is it, and how long do you think that raise takes from the day you have the data?",
    "What happens to the programme in the gap between this tranche ending and the next one landing — do you have bridge support from the institution or the other R01s?",
    "Who pays for national phase entry and the FTO opinion, and is that inside the number you quoted?"
  ],
  "confidence": "moderate"
}

Scientific Specialist — signal: caution

{
  "verdict_signal": "caution",
  "concerns": [
    "Genetic causality is solid on the loss-of-function side (CRISPR KO plus two independent siRNAs, scrambled and vehicle arms) but the rescue arm is incomplete: wild-type rescue without a catalytically-dead rescue cannot distinguish a requirement for NSMCE3 catalytic activity from a requirement for the protein as a scaffold or complex member. NSMCE3 is a non-enzymatic component of the SMC5/6 complex, so a scaffold-only phenotype is a live possibility — and if true, a small-molecule inhibitor of catalysis is the wrong modality entirely.",
    "The unmeasured paralogue is the single largest interpretability gap. Both siRNAs and the KO could produce phenotype via paralogue destabilisation or complex collapse rather than NSMCE3 loss per se; the tool compound's 12-fold selectivity against only two family members compounds this. Without paralogue transcript/protein measurement in every arm, the target is not cleanly deconvoluted.",
      "n=6 per arm chosen by budget rather than by power calculation, with no pre-specified analysis plan. For a large, clean phenotype this may be adequate; for anything in the 1.5–2 fold range it is underpowered and vulnerable to analytic flexibility. No effect size or variance is stated, so the hub cannot tell which case this is.",
    "Single lab, single set of hands, no independent replication. The Utrecht reagent request is an opportunity, not evidence. For a target with no external corroboration this is the normal state at this stage, but it should be priced as such.",
    "Human relevance rests on two primary explants — encouraging but n=2 donors, so donor-to-donor variability is unmeasurable.
